- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply downward correction of 2–5% in next 3–5 days.
- If model consistently forecasts below true price with no sentiment signal, consider mean reversion bias — adjust upward by 1–2% for next 5–7 days.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >5% from model in first 5 days, apply “lag correction” — shift forecast down by 0.5–1.5% per day for remaining period.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misjudges turning points — use sentiment momentum to adjust forecast direction 1–2 days ahead.
